title: Art Directors
description: Formulate design concepts and presentation approaches for visual productions and media, such as print, broadcasting, video, and film. Direct workers engaged in artwork or layout design.

tasks.text: Review and approve art materials, copy materials, and proofs of printed copy developed by staff members.
Review illustrative material to determine if it conforms to standards and specifications.
Research current trends and new technology, such as printing production techniques, computer software, and design trends.
Formulate basic layout design or presentation approach and specify material details, such as style and size of type, photographs, graphics, animation, video, and sound.
Mark up, paste, and complete layouts and write typography instructions to prepare materials for typesetting or printing.
Create custom illustrations or other graphic elements.
Conceptualize and help design interfaces for multimedia games, products, and devices.
Prepare detailed storyboards showing sequence and timing of story development for television production.
Work with creative directors to develop design solutions.
Present final layouts to clients for approval.
Manage own accounts and projects, working within budget and scheduling requirements.
Confer with creative, art, copywriting, or production department heads to discuss client requirements and presentation concepts and to coordinate creative activities.
Confer with clients to determine objectives, budget, background information, and presentation approaches, styles, and techniques.
Attend photo shoots and printing sessions to ensure that the products needed are obtained.
Hire, train, and direct staff members who develop design concepts into art layouts or who prepare layouts for printing.
Negotiate with printers and estimators to determine what services will be performed.

skills.name: Active Listening
skills.def: Giving full attention to what other people are saying, taking time to understand the points being made, asking questions as appropriate, and not interrupting at inappropriate times.

skills.name: Speaking
skills.def: Talking to others to convey information effectively.

skills.name: Reading Comprehension
skills.def: Understanding written sentences and paragraphs in work-related documents.

skills.name: Critical Thinking
skills.def: Using logic and reasoning to identify the strengths and weaknesses of alternative solutions, conclusions, or approaches to problems.

skills.name: Judgment and Decision Making
skills.def: Considering the relative costs and benefits of potential actions to choose the most appropriate one.

skills.name: Coordination
skills.def: Adjusting actions in relation to others' actions.

skills.name: Complex Problem Solving
skills.def: Identifying complex problems and reviewing related information to develop and evaluate options and implement solutions.

skills.name: Time Management
skills.def: Managing one's own time and the time of others.

skills.name: Writing
skills.def: Communicating effectively in writing as appropriate for the needs of the audience.

skills.name: Persuasion
skills.def: Persuading others to change their minds or behavior.

skills.name: Operations Analysis
skills.def: Analyzing needs and product requirements to create a design.

skills.name: Active Learning
skills.def: Understanding the implications of new information for both current and future problem-solving and decision-making.

skills.name: Monitoring
skills.def: Monitoring/Assessing performance of yourself, other individuals, or organizations to make improvements or take corrective action.

skills.name: Social Perceptiveness
skills.def: Being aware of others' reactions and understanding why they react as they do.

skills.name: Instructing
skills.def: Teaching others how to do something.

skills.name: Learning Strategies
skills.def: Selecting and using training/instructional methods and procedures appropriate for the situation when learning or teaching new things.

skills.name: Negotiation
skills.def: Bringing others together and trying to reconcile differences.

skills.name: Service Orientation
skills.def: Actively looking for ways to help people.

skills.name: Systems Analysis
skills.def: Determining how a system should work and how changes in conditions, operations, and the environment will affect outcomes.

skills.name: Systems Evaluation
skills.def: Identifying measures or indicators of system performance and the actions needed to improve or correct performance, relative to the goals of the system.

skills.name: Graphics or photo imaging software
skills.def: Software to draw or manipulate images. May adjust colors, add text, or apply special effects. Examples: Adobe Creative Cloud software, Adobe Illustrator, Adobe ImageReady, Adobe Photoshop.

skills.name: Video creation and editing software
skills.def: Software to enable production of video content. Examples: Adobe After Effects, Adobe Director, Adobe Premiere Pro, Apple Final Cut Pro.

skills.name: Presentation software
skills.def: Software to create presentations, speeches, or slideshows. Examples: Apple iWork Keynote, Apple Keynote, Google Slides, Microsoft PowerPoint.

skills.name: Desktop publishing software
skills.def: Software to create or edit text and graphics into documents such as books, magazines, brochures, or manuals. Examples: Adobe InDesign, Quark enterprise publishing software, QuarkXPress.

skills.name: Graphical user interface development software
skills.def: Software to create or maintain applications which interact with users through a graphical interface. Examples: Figma.

skills.name: Office suite software
skills.def: Software to provide word processing, spreadsheet, e-mail, presentations, or data management capabilities. Examples: Microsoft Office software.
